fields.statement: QA claude-code-6b4d6ff8 at fac284e5, hands-on with the built binary (go build -trimpath -o $TMPDIR/rhiza-qa ./cmd/rhiza): a scratch root (rhiza root init) with alpha and beta initialised and bare a plain git checkout, each registered with rhiza project add; fixture run journals in alpha (a failed run at 01:00, a question at 03:00) and beta (a question at 02:00, a stale run); rhiza daemon set paused=true, web.host 127.0.0.1, web.port 18931; rhiza daemon --permission-mode manual run from alpha, then curl against http://127.0.0.1:18931. One listener answered for every project: / 200 (home alpha), /p/alpha/ and /p/beta/ 200, /p/alpha/runs, /p/beta/roadmap 200, /p/alpha 301, /p/nope/ and /p/bare/ 404. Running rhiza init in bare with the daemon still up made /p/bare/ answer 200 with no restart, and the switcher then listed bare.

QA claude-code-6b4d6ff8 at fac284e5, hands-on with the built binary (go build -trimpath -o $TMPDIR/rhiza-qa ./cmd/rhiza): a scratch root (rhiza root init) with alpha and beta initialised and bare a plain git checkout, each registered with rhiza project add; fixture run journals in alpha (a failed run at 01:00, a question at 03:00) and beta (a question at 02:00, a stale run); rhiza daemon set paused=true, web.host 127.0.0.1, web.port 18931; rhiza daemon --permission-mode manual run from alpha, then curl against http://127.0.0.1:18931. GET /projects listed alpha (1 waiting on you · 2 in inbox), bare (not initialised, no counts or health) and beta (2 waiting on you · 1 in inbox). Each project had its own health pill: unknown at first, unhealthy after the first poll, which matches rhiza health in that project (bad check, as the model was not rendered). Rows linked /p/alpha/, /p/bare/ and /p/beta/. The home is served at /projects and linked from every page's nav; / itself is still the home project's overview (see the QA findings).

QA claude-code-6b4d6ff8 at fac284e5, hands-on with the built binary (go build -trimpath -o $TMPDIR/rhiza-qa ./cmd/rhiza): a scratch root (rhiza root init) with alpha and beta initialised and bare a plain git checkout, each registered with rhiza project add; fixture run journals in alpha (a failed run at 01:00, a question at 03:00) and beta (a question at 02:00, a stale run); rhiza daemon set paused=true, web.host 127.0.0.1, web.port 18931; rhiza daemon --permission-mode manual run from alpha, then curl against http://127.0.0.1:18931. GET /inbox listed the items oldest first across projects: alpha Alpha failing work (failed, 01:00), beta Which beta colour? (02:00), alpha Which alpha store? (03:00). Each row had a rz-project-tag span with its project and linked /p/<project>/runs/<run>, and each link answered 200. A question journal added to beta while the daemon ran showed up on /inbox, tagged beta.

QA claude-code-6b4d6ff8 at fac284e5, hands-on with the built binary (go build -trimpath -o $TMPDIR/rhiza-qa ./cmd/rhiza): a scratch root (rhiza root init) with alpha and beta initialised and bare a plain git checkout, each registered with rhiza project add; fixture run journals in alpha (a failed run at 01:00, a question at 03:00) and beta (a question at 02:00, a stale run); rhiza daemon set paused=true, web.host 127.0.0.1, web.port 18931; rhiza daemon --permission-mode manual run from alpha, then curl against http://127.0.0.1:18931. /p/alpha/, /p/alpha/roadmap, /p/alpha/runs, /p/beta/runs/<run> and /p/beta/changes/<cs> each showed only their own project's change sets and runs. Each header had nav.rz-switcher with All projects and every initialised project. The links kept the page kind: roadmap went to /p/beta/roadmap, runs to /p/beta/runs, and a run or change set detail page went to the other project's runs or roadmap list. The current project was marked aria-current. Another project's run or change set ID under /p/alpha/ gave 404, and so did /p/nope/events. body data-rz-base=/p/beta. With /p/alpha/events and /p/beta/events open, a new beta journal sent inbox and run events only on beta's stream; alpha's got only its daemon health event.
